exposure: major fusion defects (unicornuate, bicornuate and didelphys)
minor fusion defects (arcuate, septate and t-shaped)
cohort: 158 patients with a singleton pregnancy and a uterine anomaly, compared to 158 randomly selected unexposed singleton pregnancies
finding: The incidence of adverse pregnancy outcomes and cesarean delivery is increased in patients with minor fusion defects and is further increased in patients with major fusion defects.
mod_finding: The incidence of Cesarean delivery was higher in patients with both minor and major uterine fusion defects.
